detail.body: ## Purpose Currently LoRA Loading for Per Request needs to first sequentially **load all the LoRA layers** before **beginning Pre-Fill**. This adds significant overhead in TTFT. However, **Pre-Fill** is a layer by layer process and for large enough input tokens(**> 1000 tokens**) it is **longer than LoRA Loading time**. If we run **LoRA loading and Compute in separate streams(CUDA or otherwise)** we can hid significant part of the LoRA loading time with **Sync points** in each LoRA layer of the forward pass to make sure the LoRA layer is loaded. The above process allows for **E2E TTFT to be nearly ~28% lower** ## Test Plan ### **Ran LoRA test cases for 3D MoE models** ``` pytest tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py pytest tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py pytest tests/lora/test_lora_async_loading.py ``` ### **Benchmarked e2e TTFT when loading LoRAs from CPU to GPU** Server command (loads 8 LoRAs, with only one on CPU, causing frequent swapping in from CPU to GPU during runtime): ``` vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b \ --trust-remote-code --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-cpu-loras 8 \ -tp=1 --port 8001 --lora-modules \ lora1=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora2=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora3=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora4=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora5=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora6=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora7=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 lora8=./gpt-oss-20b-coding-rank32-lr1e-5 --max-lora-rank 32 \ --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching ``` **Benchmark command:** ``` vllm bench serve --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --ignore-eos --random-range-ratio=0.05 --random-input-len=1600 --random-output-len=200 --max-concurrency 1 --lora-modules lora1 lora2 lora3 lora4 lora5 lora6 lora7 lora8 --num-prompts 100 --port 8001 ``` Results +"""
+Tests for LoRA Async Loading with CUDA stream-based pipelining.
+"""
+

+    if current_platform.is_cuda_alike()
+    else ["cpu"]
+)
+
+DEFAULT_DTYPE = torch.get_default_dtype()
+
+
+def create_lora_manager(dummy_model, device):
+    """Helper to create LoRAModelManager with standard test config."""
+    return LoRAModelManager(
+        dummy_model,
+        2,
+        2,
+        2,
+        LoRAConfig(
+            max_lora_rank=8, max_cpu_loras=8, max_loras=8, lora_dtype=DEFAULT_DTYPE

+        device=device,
+    )
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", DEVICES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_enabled", [True, False])
+def test_cuda_stream_initialization(dist_init, dummy_model, device, async_enabled):
+    """Verify CUDA loading stream and lora_ready flags are created
+    when async loading is enabled, and absent when disabled."""
+
+    if async_enabled and not current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
+        pytest.skip("Async LoRA loading requires CUDA")
+
+    env_value = "1" if async_enabled else "0"
+    with patch.dict(os.environ, {"VLLM_LORA_REQUEST_ASYNC_LOADING_CUDA": env_value}):
+        manager = create_lora_manager(dummy_model, device)
+
+        if async_enabled:
+            # Loading stream must exist
+            assert hasattr(manager, "lora_loading_stream")
+            assert isinstance(manager.lora_loading_stream, torch.cuda.Stream)
+
+            # Every LoRA module should have a lora_ready flag
+            for module_name, module in manager.modules.items():
+                assert hasattr(module, "lora_ready"), (
+                    f"Module {module_name} missing lora_ready flag"
+                )
+                assert module.lora_ready.dtype == torch.uint32
+        else:
+            assert not hasattr(manager, "lora_loading_stream")
+

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The padding logic for `FusedMoEWithLoRA` appears to have a bug. It incorrectly uses the buffer shape of `w13_lora_a_stacked[0]` for all `lora_a` components, including `w2`. This will lead to a shape mismatch if the hidden size and intermediate size are different, which is usually the case. A similar issue exists for `lora_b` where `w3` incorrectly uses the buffer for `w1`.

While this might work by chance if some shapes align, it's not robust. I've provided a more explicit and correct implementation that uses the correct buffer shapes for each component (`w1`, `w2`, `w3`), ensuring the padding is always correct.

```python
        if isinstance(module, FusedMoEWithLoRA):
            if isinstance(module_lora.lora_a, list):
                # lora_a order: [w1, w2, w3] per expert
                # w1/w3 (gate/up) use _slice_w13, w2 (down) uses _slice_w2
                lora_a_buffers = [
                    module.w13_lora_a_stacked[0],
                    module.w2_lora_a_stacked[0],
                    module.w13_lora_a_stacked[1],
                ]
                lora_a_slice_fns = [
                    module._slice_w13_a,
                    module._slice_w2_a,
                    module._slice_w13_a,
                ]
                for i in range(len(module_lora.lora_a)):
                    if module_lora.lora_a[i] is not None:
                        module_lora.lora_a[i] = pad_to_buffer(
                            module_lora.lora_a[i],
                            lora_a_buffers[i].shape,
                            is_moe=True,
                            slice_fn=lora_a_slice_fns[i],
                        )

                lora_b_buffers = [
                    module.w13_lora_b_stacked[0],
                    module.w2_lora_b_stacked[0],
                    module.w13_lora_b_stacked[1],
                ]
                lora_b_slice_fns = [
                    module._slice_w13_b,
                    module._slice_w2_b,
                    module._slice_w13_b,
                ]
                for i in range(len(module_lora.lora_b)):
                    if module_lora.lora_b[i] is not None:
                        module_lora.lora_b[i] = pad_to_buffer(
                            module_lora.lora_b[i],
                            lora_b_buffers[i].shape,
                            is_moe=True,
                            slice_fn=lora_b_slice_fns[i],
                        )
            return
```
